title: Configuration export may copy provider keys to shared Documents
description: The user-initiated export copies the active profile patch or legacy settings file verbatim into shared Documents. The engine warns that profile patches may contain provider keys, while the UI says the export contains no API keys and does not show the warning hint. Actual keys and cross-app readability are unverified.
claimed_root_cause: The active configuration is copied to shared storage without redaction while the UI gives an unconditional no-keys assurance; actual secret presence and external access depend on device state.

trace.description: The user can invoke the configuration export from the settings UI.
The native handler selects and exports the active configuration.
The selected file is copied to shared exports/config without content redaction.

evidence.description: The export source is the active profile patch when present or migrated, otherwise legacy settings.
The source file is copied to the export destination.
The native result warns that the active configuration may contain provider keys.
The UI states that the export contains no API keys.

blockers: The checked-in source does not establish whether an installed active configuration contains provider credentials.
No particular unauthorized reader is evidenced; Android storage policy and other-app permissions determine access.
No approved isolated Android device was available for a synthetic export and cross-principal read check.

validation_plan.local: With an approved isolated device, export a synthetic configuration containing a nonsecret marker and compare the copied bytes; test read access with ordinary and broad-storage test apps only. Do not read or copy real provider credentials.
validation_plan.deployment: Have the owner verify the active profile's credential presence without recording values, and confirm what users see and which test identities can read a synthetic exported file on the supported Android version.
